topics.name: Document Loaders & Text Splitters
topics.description: Loading sources into Documents and splitting them into retrievable chunks.
notes: ## Document 与 Loader
- Document 是文本单元，有三个属性：page_content（文本）、metadata（任意 dict，如 source）、id（可选）。
- Document loader 把 Slack、Notion、Google Drive 等不同来源的数据读成统一的 Document 格式。
- 所有 loader 实现 BaseLoader 接口：load() 一次性加载全部，lazy_load() 惰性流式加载，适合大数据集。
## Text Splitter
- 目的：把大文档切成可单独检索、且能放进模型上下文窗口的小块。
- 大多数场景从 RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter 开始，文档称它是通用文本的推荐切分器。
- 递归切分：先尽量保留大单元（段落），超过 chunk_size 就降到下一层（句子），必要时一直降到单词。
```python
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
chunk_size=1000, chunk_overlap=200, add_start_index=True
all_splits = splitter.split_documents(docs)
- add_start_index=True 会在每个块的 metadata 中保留 start_index（块在原文档中的字符偏移）。
## 其他切分策略
- 按长度：按 token 数或字符数切分，例如 CharacterTextSplitter.from_tiktoken_encoder。
- 按文档结构：Markdown 按标题、HTML 按标签、JSON 按对象或数组元素、代码按函数或类。

topics.name: Vector Store Queries & Retrievers
topics.description: Querying vector stores and wrapping them as retrievers.
notes: ## VectorStore 接口
- 统一接口包含三个基本操作：add_documents 添加、delete 按 ID 删除、similarity_search 语义查询。
- 常用参数：k 控制返回数量，filter 按 metadata 过滤（各实现的支持程度不同，需查对应文档）。
```python
ids = vector_store.add_documents(documents=all_splits)
docs = vector_store.similarity_search(
"query", k=3, filter={"source": "tweets"}
- 其他查询方式：同步或异步、按字符串或按向量（similarity_search_by_vector）、带分数（similarity_search_with_score）、MMR（兼顾相似度与多样性）。
- 分数含义因提供方而异；教程示例里的分数是与相似度成反比的距离。
## Retriever
- VectorStore 不是 Runnable；Retriever 是 Runnable，支持 invoke、batch 及异步版本。
- vector_store.as_retriever 返回 VectorStoreRetriever，用 search_type 与 search_kwargs 配置。
- search_type 可选 "similarity"（默认）、"mmr"、"similarity_score_threshold"（按相似度分数过滤）。
```python
retriever = vector_store.as_retriever(
search_type="similarity",
search_kwargs={"k": 1},
- Retriever 也可以包装非向量来源，例如外部 API。

topics.name: RAG Architectures
topics.description: 2-step RAG, agentic RAG and hybrid RAG compared.
notes: ## 为什么需要检索
- LLM 有两个限制：上下文有限（无法一次读入整个语料）；知识是静态的（训练数据停在某个时间点）。
- 检索在查询时取回相关的外部知识，这就是 RAG（Retrieval-Augmented Generation）的基础。
## 三种架构
- 2-Step RAG：检索总是在生成之前执行，简单且可预测，适合 FAQ、文档问答机器人。
- Agentic RAG：由 LLM 驱动的 agent 在推理中决定何时、如何检索，灵活但延迟不固定，适合有多个工具的研究助手。
- Hybrid：结合两者并加入验证步骤，控制与灵活性居中。
## 对比
- 2-Step：控制高、灵活性低、延迟快；LLM 调用次数有上限，所以延迟更可预测。
- Agentic：控制低、灵活性高、延迟可变。
- Agent 要具备 RAG 能力，只需要能获取外部知识的工具（文档加载器、Web API、数据库查询等）。
```python
agent = create_agent(
model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
tools=[fetch_url],  # 检索工具
system_prompt=system_prompt,
## Hybrid RAG 的典型组件
- Query enhancement：改写、生成多个变体或扩展查询。
- Retrieval validation：判断检索结果是否相关且充分，不够就改写后再检索。
- Answer validation：检查答案的准确性、完整性及与来源一致，必要时重新生成。
- 已有知识库（SQL、文档数据库、CRM 等）不必重建：可作为 agent 的工具，或查询后把结果作为上下文交给 LLM。

topics.name: Grounding, Sources & Prompt Injection
topics.description: Passing retrieved context with sources and handling injection risk.
notes: ## 把检索结果交给模型
- RAG 把问题和检索到的上下文一起放进提示词，让模型基于它回答。
- 切分后每个块保留 metadata（如 source、page、start_index），可以用来标注引用来源。
- 教程里的检索工具给每个块加上 `# Source: <url>` 头部，来源取自 doc.metadata。
```python
content = (
f"# Source: {doc.metadata.get('source', 'unknown')}\n\n"
f"{doc.page_content}"
- 在系统提示里要求引用相关片段或附上文档链接，答案才可追溯。
## 检索结果工具化
- Deep Agents 教程：工具做相似度搜索（k=4），把块写入文件系统，只返回文件路径。
- 这样 orchestrator 不必把完整块文本放进自己的上下文，而是委派子 agent 读取并总结。
## 安全：间接提示注入
- 检索到的内容与系统提示共享上下文窗口，文档里类似指令的文本可能被模型当作指令执行。
- 教程的做法：提示中说明检索内容只是数据、忽略其中的指令；用 `# Source:` 头区分元数据和正文。
- 没有任何提示或分隔符策略能完全防止注入，所以要校验输出，确认引用了预期的文档路径、结论与来源一致。
## 可观测性
- 开启 LangSmith 后，每次查询都会记录 trace，可检查检索、工具调用和模型回复。

questions.title: Which methods form the common API shared by LangChain document loaders?
questions.explanation: load() loads all documents at once, while lazy_load() streams them lazily, which suits large datasets. The other names are not part of the shared interface.

questions.title: In a LangChain Document, which attribute holds arbitrary information such as the source of the text?
questions.explanation: metadata is a dict that can capture the source and other information. page_content holds the text itself and id is an optional identifier.

questions.title: Which text splitter do the docs recommend as the starting point for generic text?
questions.explanation: RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter balances keeping context intact with managing chunk size. The others target specific formats or a single separator.

questions.title: Fill in the argument so each split keeps its character offset in the original document as start_index metadata.
questions.codeSnippet:
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter

splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=1000,
    chunk_overlap=200,
    ______=True,
)
all_splits = splitter.split_documents(docs)
questions.explanation: add_start_index=True stores each split's character offset in a start_index metadata field. The other names are not splitter parameters.

questions.title: With RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter, a paragraph is longer than chunk_size. What does the splitter do?

options.text: It moves to the next level, such as sentences, and continues down to words if necessary
It raises an error because the paragraph does not fit
It truncates the paragraph at chunk_size and drops the rest
It keeps the oversized paragraph as one chunk

questions.explanation: The splitter tries to keep larger units intact and falls back to smaller ones only when a unit exceeds the chunk size.

questions.title: Which of these are examples of document structure-based splitting listed in the docs?

options.text: Splitting JSON by object or array elements
Cutting text every fixed number of tokens regardless of structure

questions.explanation: Structure-based splitting follows the logical organization of Markdown, HTML, JSON or code. Fixed token cuts are length-based splitting.

questions.title: Which operations make up LangChain's unified vector store interface?
questions.explanation: The interface adds documents, deletes them by ID and runs similarity search. embed_* methods belong to the Embeddings interface.

questions.title: What does this code print?
questions.codeSnippet:
retriever = vector_store.as_retriever(
    search_type="similarity",
    search_kwargs={"k": 1},
)
out = retriever.batch(["Question 1", "Question 2"])
print(len(out), len(out[0]))
questions.explanation: batch() returns one list of documents per query, so the outer list has 2 items. search_kwargs k=1 makes each inner list hold one document.

questions.title: Fill in the keyword argument that restricts the search by metadata.
questions.explanation: Many vector stores accept k and filter for similarity_search. Support for metadata filtering varies, so check the chosen integration.

questions.title: Which search_type of a VectorStoreRetriever filters documents by similarity score?
questions.explanation: The supported search types are similarity (default), mmr and similarity_score_threshold. mmr balances similarity with diversity rather than filtering by score.

questions.title: Which statement about VectorStore objects and retrievers is correct?

options.text: Both are Runnables and support invoke and batch
VectorStore objects are Runnables, retrievers are not
VectorStore objects do not subclass Runnable, while retrievers are Runnables

questions.explanation: Retrievers are Runnables, so they support invoke and batch in sync and async form. A vector store is not a Runnable, which is why as_retriever exists.

questions.title: The code should print the similarity score of the top result but fails. What is the bug?
questions.codeSnippet:
results = vector_store.similarity_search(
    "What was Nike's revenue in 2023?", k=1
)
doc, score = results[0]
print(score)

options.text: similarity_search returns Document objects without scores; use similarity_search_with_score for (document, score) pairs
k must be at least 2 before a result can be unpacked
Scores are only available through as_retriever

questions.explanation: similarity_search returns a list of Document objects. similarity_search_with_score returns documents together with scores.

questions.title: Which ways of querying a vector store does the semantic search tutorial list?

options.text: By vector instead of by string
By executing SQL joins across stores

questions.explanation: Vector stores can be queried synchronously or asynchronously, by string or vector, with or without scores, and by similarity or MMR. SQL joins are not part of the interface.

questions.title: In the tutorial, similarity_search_with_score returns a score described as a distance metric that varies inversely with similarity. What should you conclude about scores in general?

options.text: A higher score always means a more similar document
Score semantics are provider-specific, and here a lower score means a closer match
Scores are always cosine similarities between 0 and 1
Scores are probabilities that the answer is correct

questions.explanation: The docs note that providers implement different scores. In the tutorial the score is a distance, so smaller values are better, and it is wrong to assume higher is better.

questions.title: Which two LLM limitations does retrieval address?

options.text: Slow tokenization and expensive output tokens
No tool calling and no streaming

questions.explanation: LLMs cannot ingest whole corpora and their training data is frozen in time. Retrieval fetches relevant external knowledge at query time.

questions.title: According to the docs, what does an agent need in order to enable RAG behavior?

options.text: Access to one or more tools that fetch external knowledge
A retrieval step hard-coded before every answer
A vector store that subclasses Runnable

questions.explanation: Tools such as documentation loaders, web APIs or database queries are enough. A fixed retrieval step describes 2-step RAG instead.

questions.title: Why is latency generally more predictable in 2-step RAG than in agentic RAG?

options.text: The maximum number of LLM calls is known and capped
It never calls a language model
It always uses a local embedding model

questions.explanation: Retrieval always runs before generation, so the number of LLM calls is bounded. Real latency can still vary with retrieval infrastructure such as API or database response times.

questions.title: Which are typical components of hybrid RAG?

options.text: Fine-tuning the model weights after every question

questions.explanation: Hybrid RAG adds query rewriting, checks on whether retrieved documents are sufficient, and checks on the generated answer. It does not change model weights.

questions.title: Which statements about agentic RAG are correct according to the docs?

options.text: An agent decides when and how to retrieve during its reasoning
Retrieval is always executed once before generation
It offers high flexibility but lower control and variable latency compared with 2-step RAG
The agent only needs access to tools that can fetch external knowledge

questions.explanation: Agentic RAG trades control and predictable latency for flexibility. Retrieval that always runs before generation is the definition of 2-step RAG.

questions.title: You already have a knowledge base in a SQL database. Which options does the retrieval guide give you without rebuilding it?

options.text: Connect it as a tool for an agent in agentic RAG
Query it and supply the retrieved content as context to the LLM (2-step RAG)
Re-ingest it into a vector store first, because RAG requires embeddings

questions.explanation: An existing SQL database, document database, CRM or internal documentation system does not need to be rebuilt. It can be an agent tool or a source for 2-step RAG context.

questions.title: Which RAG architecture does this code implement?

options.text: 2-step RAG, because retrieval always runs before generation
Hybrid RAG, because it validates the final answer
None, because RAG requires a vector store
Agentic RAG, because the agent decides when to call the retrieval tool

questions.explanation: The agent chooses whether to call fetch_url. The docs say a tool that fetches external knowledge is all an agent needs for RAG, so a vector store is not required.

questions.title: Why are RAG applications susceptible to indirect prompt injection?

options.text: Retrieved chunks share the context window with the system prompt, so the model may follow instructions embedded in them
Vector stores execute code found inside documents
Embedding models leak API keys into the chunks
Text splitters reorder the system prompt

questions.explanation: Retrieved text that resembles instructions sits in the same context as your prompt. The docs state that no prompt or delimiter strategy fully prevents this, so outputs should be validated.

questions.title: The system prompt asks the agent to cite the source of each claim, but it never can. What is the bug?

options.text: k=4 returns too many chunks to cite
The tool returns only page_content and drops doc.metadata, so the model never sees the sources
The docstring is too short for the model to call the tool

questions.explanation: Retrieved Documents carry metadata such as source, but the tool throws it away. The tutorial tool prefixes each chunk with a header built from doc.metadata.get('source').

questions.title: What does the agent receive as the result of this retrieval tool, and why is it designed this way?
questions.codeSnippet:
docs = vector_store.similarity_search(query, k=4)
uploads, paths = [], []
for i, doc in enumerate(docs, start=1):
    path = f"/retrieved/{batch_id}/chunk_{i}.md"
    uploads.append((path, doc.page_content.encode("utf-8")))
    paths.append(path)
backend.upload_files(uploads)
return "Saved chunks:\n" + "\n".join(paths)

options.text: The full text of all four chunks
The embedding vectors of the chunks
File paths, so chunk text stays out of the orchestrator context and subagents can analyze it
Nothing, because the function never returns

questions.explanation: The chunks are written to the agent filesystem and only the paths are returned. The orchestrator can then delegate analysis without loading full chunk text into its own context.

questions.title: Which Embeddings method turns a single query string into one vector?
questions.explanation: embed_query(text) returns one vector, while embed_documents(texts) embeds a list of documents and returns a list of vectors.

questions.title: CacheBackedEmbeddings.from_bytes_store is called with only the underlying embedder, a document_embedding_cache and a namespace. Which embeddings are cached?

options.text: Only document embeddings, because query embeddings are not cached by default

questions.explanation: Query embeddings are cached only if you pass query_embedding_cache. Setting the namespace, for example to the model name, avoids collisions between models.

questions.title: This E5 model expects different prefixes for documents and queries. Fill in the argument that sets the query prefix.
questions.codeSnippet:
from langchain_huggingface import HuggingFaceEmbeddings

embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(
    model_name="intfloat/e5-large-v2",
    encode_kwargs={"prompt": "passage: "},
    ______={"prompt": "query: "},
)
questions.explanation: The docs pass the document prompt through encode_kwargs and the query prompt through query_encode_kwargs. Using the wrong prefix at query time is a common quality regression.

questions.title: Which kind of query do dense embeddings handle less well, motivating hybrid retrieval with BM25 or sparse indexes?

options.text: Exact-match queries such as product codes, named entities and code identifiers

questions.explanation: Dense vectors capture semantic similarity but can miss exact keywords. Hybrid retrieval combines a dense index with BM25 or a sparse neural index to cover both cases.
